transcript.answer: Lore's web UI uses one WebSocket per browser tab, served by lore-api at `/api/ws` (ADR-048, PR #2122, 2026-09-23). It replaced the run page's earlier Server-Sent Events stream (ADR-037). The socket carries JSON text frames and multiplexes named channels, each with a client-chosen channel id. The `run` channel forwards an assembly run's pod events and transcript. Access to it uses a token minted by `POST /api/assembly-runs/{id}/stream-token`. The `plan` channel tunnels the plan editor's Hocuspocus collaboration bytes to the same collaboration server. The collab-token handshake stays inside the tunnel. The web-ui keeps the socket in a provider above every page, so navigating from a plan to its run keeps the connection. On the server, one feed per run subscribes once to the Postgres NOTIFY hub. That means N viewers cost one re-read per notification. The browser connects directly to lore-api's public host, configured via `LORE_WS_URL` (`wss://<host>/api/ws`).

judgements.reason: The answer states the single WebSocket per tab at lore-api's /api/ws, multiplexed named channels with JSON frames (run and plan), and that it replaced the earlier per-run SSE stream; it omits the 'runs' channel but contradicts nothing.
